summary: Snap To Mouse tab: select an object, hover the Scene view, press a key and it teleports to what the mouse points at.
overview: A placement tool for the tedious part of dressing a level: getting props to actually sit on the ground. Select the object, point the mouse where you want it, press the key, done — no hand-editing Y positions, no dragging against a gizmo and hoping.
It is a ONE-SHOT action rather than a held-key drag or a click-to-place mode, which is what makes it safe to leave the tab open while you work: nothing happens until you press the key.

walkthrough.step: Select a GameObject in the Hierarchy.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: If nothing is selected the tab says so with a warning rather than silently doing nothing when you press the key.

walkthrough.step: Set Surface Mask to the geometry you want to land on.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: Only those layers are raycast, so a prop will not snap onto a trigger volume or another prop unless you allow it.

walkthrough.step: Hover the Scene view and press V (or whatever you set as the Snap Key).
walkthrough.whatYouSee: The object jumps once to the surface under the mouse, keeping its current rotation.

walkthrough.step: Tick 'Also align rotation to the surface normal' and press again on a slope.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: The object's up axis rotates to match the surface as well as moving there, taking the minimal rotation from its current orientation — what you want for a prop that should sit flush on a ramp or hillside.

useCases: Scattering rocks, crates and foliage across uneven terrain without touching a single Y value.
Dropping a prop precisely onto a ledge or stair tread that is awkward to hit with a drag gizmo.
Re-seating props that ended up floating after terrain was re-sculpted under them.

gotchas.title: 3D only, by design — no fixed-plane fallback
gotchas.body: It always raycasts real colliders. A measuring point can be abstract, but a snapped prop should not float in mid-air, and a fallback plane would let the snap land somewhere with no real surface under it. If the mouse is not over collidable geometry, nothing moves.

gotchas.title: It snaps the object's pivot, not its base
gotchas.body: The transform lands on the surface, so a prop whose pivot sits at its centre will end up half-buried. Prefabs intended for this want their pivot at the foot of the model.
